title: onboarding-friction-mapper-and-inline-labs
creator: Leah Park
description: Goal: Reduce first-session friction for new Redwood Console users by introducing a lightweight "onboarding friction mapper" and a set of inline labs (micro-tutorials) that appear contextually in empty states and dashboards. The mapper is a small diagnostic that surfaces why a user might be blocked (missing secrets/KMS, no projects, no models, no data) and then exposes 1-click micro-labs to complete the most common tasks. This ticket covers UX flows, high-fidelity prototypes, and two rounds of quick moderated usability tests with 6-8 participants each. Deliverables: Figma prototype, annotated interaction spec, copy table, accessibility checklist, and a short recording of the usability sessions with recommendation notes.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype for friction mapper and three inline lab types (create-project, connect-kms, seed-sample-requests) linked from this ticket
Annotated interaction spec describing triggers, fallback behavior, and analytics events (open, completion, dismiss)
Micro-copy table with primary CTA, secondary CTA, and tooltip variants for A/B testing
Two rounds of moderated usability tests documented: findings, severity, and at least 5 prioritised design changes
Handoff-ready assets: components, variants, and CSS tokens; developer checklist for accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, color contrast)
Engineering dependencies documented and owned (ENG-20098 for empty state gating, ENG-20112 for in-console onboarding events)
PM sign-off and inclusion in console-2025.04 release plan
tasks: Draft diagnostic flow map and failure categories (Leah)
Build Figma prototype and link annotations
Prepare copy variants and tone guide with Content (review: Ana Ruiz)
Conduct usability round 1 (prototype) and synthesize notes
Iterate designs based on round 1, run round 2
Create accessibility checklist and component tokens
Handoff package and sync with ENG owners (handoff meeting)

comments: 2025-02-14 - Leah Park: Kickoff notes uploaded. Initial hypothesis: >50% of new signups fail to progress due to missing project scaffolding or KMS connectivity. Figma skeleton created: https://www.figma.com/file/ABC123/onboarding-friction-mapper
2025-02-19 - Mateo Singh: Iteration 1 added: three inline labs (project, KMS, seed dataset). Started micro-copy variants. Shared first flows with PM Ana for feedback.

2025-02-24 - Ana Ruiz (PM): Suggested making the friction mapper non-modal and dismissible to avoid interrupting power users. Also proposed telemetry events: mapper_shown, lab_started, lab_completed, lab_dismissed.

2025-02-27 - Usability Lab 1: 7 participants (mixed dev/pm roles). Key findings: users want a quick 'skip and generate sample' path; KMS setup is perceived as high-friction—add screenshots and expected time estimate. Action: add 'try with demo keys' inline lab and simplify KMS lab copy.

2025-03-02 - Design Review: Reviewed with UX leadership. Decision: prioritize non-blocking inline labs in dashboards and postpone a full guided tour. Agreed to run A/B test on primary CTA wording ('Get started' vs 'Try with demo'). Added ENG dependencies: ENG-20098, ENG-20112.

2025-03-02 - Mateo Singh: Updated Figma link with round 1 tweaks: https://www.figma.com/file/ABC123/onboarding-friction-mapper?node-id=452%3A12. Preparing usability plan for round 2 (target 6 participants).
